newsitem.title: KENYA: Barclays Kenya sells investment firm stake.
newsitem.headline: Barclays Kenya sells investment firm stake.

text.p: Barclays Bank of Kenya has sold its 11 percent shareholding in National Industrial Credit, brokers said on Wednesday.

They said that Barclays had offered the 11 percent or 4,827,295 shares for sale on the three-day special lots board. They said the completion of the deal, at 52 shillings per share, was likely to be announced on Thursday.

The shares were the balance not sold when Barclays offered to sell 51 percent of its holding in the investment company in 1994. Brokers said Barclays wanted to get out of National Industrial Credit because of a perceived conflict of interest.
"National Industrial Credit wants to convert into a bank and Barclays sees its activities as in conflict with its core business. That is why it wants to sell," a broker said.
Since the 1994 flotation of the Barclays stake, the National Industrial Credit stock has eased, closing at 40 shillings on Wednesday from an offer price of 52 at flotation.

"The matter is quite controversial. The National Industrial Credit shares have dropped drastically since the offer. Now other investors are asking why they can't get out at the price of 52. The market appears unfair," a senior dealer said.
The main question appeared to be that Barclays had found a buyer to purchase their 11 percent holding at a premium when National Industrial Credit has held steady in the 40-range.
"People have lost money in this stock. From 52, no one is getting anything near there now," a floor dealer said.
"Suddenly, there is a buyer at 52. That has caused so much speculation on the market," the floor dealer added.

Dealers also questioned where local investors could get 251,019,340 shillings required to buy the special block of National Industrial Credit shares at 52 shillings per share and speculated on who the buyers might be.
"Whatever the speculation, no rules have so far been breached," an official at a leading brokerage house said. "But that does not mean that there will not be many complaints."
The index fell 24.93 points to 3053.12 while turnover was posted at 6.430 million shillings at 208,703 shares from 11.477 million shillings on 375,517 shares on Tuesday.
